label: Connecticut: applicability
citation: Conn. Gen. Stat. §§42-515–42-517; PA26-64 §12 (definitions effective October 1, 2026)
note: Editorial summary checked against primary law on October 26, 2026. The 35,000-consumer, sensitive-data, and offering-for-sale applicability routes remain in force. Apply the definitions effective October 1, 2026 under PA26-64 §12. PA26-100 §66 repealed PA26-64 §§11 and 16; the replacement surveillance-pricing provisions take effect July 1, 2027 under PA26-130 §11. This guide assesses the comprehensive privacy act, not the separate data-broker, genetic-testing, or surveillance-pricing regimes.
body: Does the assessment involve personal data of Connecticut consumers?

Does ANY current route hold: it conducts business in Connecticut OR targets products/services to Connecticut residents, AND controlled or processed at least 35,000 consumers’ personal data in the preceding calendar year (excluding payment-only data); OR it controls or processes a consumer’s sensitive data (excluding payment-only data); OR it offers consumers’ personal data for sale in trade or commerce?

Connecticut residents in an individual or household context, excluding employment and commercial roles. The 35,000 limb and sensitive-data limb exclude processing solely to complete a payment transaction.

Publicly accessible information is not automatically excluded. The October 2026 definition excludes, among other things, public information combined with personal data and information a consumer restricted to a specific audience. See PA26-64 §12 for the full definitions.
Measuring period: 35,000 route: preceding calendar year. Sensitive-data and offering-for-sale routes have no minimum count or revenue-share test.
